subject: Private offer packaging options & channel margin cap — Cloudwise
messages:
From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@cloudwise.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cloudwise.com
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer inquiry — packaging options & reseller margin cap

Hi Connor / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week — Cloudwise is interested in moving forward with a private offer across AWS and GCP, but procurement needs clarity on a few commercial items before we draft an SOW: 

1) Packaging: they want a combined multi-sku private offer (compute + inference tokens + managed support). Are we able to present both a consolidated SKU (single list price) and an itemized SKU option to their billing team?

2) Channel margin cap: their reseller (EdgeBridge) requires an explicit cap in the PO. Procurement asked whether Redwood can set a maximum channel margin percentage on the private offer (they mentioned 22% as a target).

3) Billing/crediting: they asked how overage credits and marketplace passback are handled across regions — specifically how we attribute list price vs net revenue for partner commissions.

Attached is a short requirements doc from procurement (cloudwise_requirements.pdf). They'd like options and a sample pricing matrix by EOD Monday if possible.

Can you confirm feasibility and a recommended structure?

Best,
Alyssa
Head of Procurement
Cloudwise Systems

(Attachment: cloudwise_requirements.pdf)

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@cloudwise.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — packaging options & reseller margin cap

Alyssa — thanks for the clear ask and the requirements doc. Quick summary of what we can do and next steps: 

- Packaging: we can support both a consolidated SKU (single charge line) and an itemized invoice. For marketplace private offers (AWS/GCP) the consolidated SKU is easier for their finance team but requires mapping back to the marketplace SKU for reporting.

- Channel margin cap: we don't typically hard-cap an external partner margin on the PO itself, but we can model the private offer pricing such that the effective margin is limited (i.e., set a list price that leaves a controllable reseller uplift). If procurement needs a contractual cap language, legal can include a clause referencing an agreed-upon maximum reseller uplift for the PO.

- Billing/crediting: overages are handled via usage true-ups. We can show an example waterfall: gross list -> marketplace fees -> reseller uplift -> net revenue. That should address how commissions are calculated.

I'll attach a quick pricing model (pricing_model_v2.xlsx) and our private offer template for their procurement/legal to review. Ben — can you confirm recommended margin guardrails and whether legal needs a specific clause? Irene — can you confirm any SKU-mapping constraints for GCP marketplace?

Connor Obrien
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: pricing_model_v2.xlsx, private_offer_template.docx)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, Alyssa Turner <alyssa@cloudwise.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 6 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — packaging options & reseller margin cap

Thanks Alyssa / Connor. A few practical recommendations from the channel/ops side: 

- Margin cap approach: instead of embedding a hard cap in the PO, propose an explicit reseller uplift table (example below) tied to list-price bands. That gives procurement visibility and control without creating billing complexity. Example:
  * List price band 0-250k -> reseller uplift <= 25%
  * 250k-750k -> uplift <= 22%
  * >750k -> uplift <= 20% (volume-based concession)

- Consolidated SKU tradeoffs: consolidated SKU = simpler external billing but reduces transparency for passback. If EdgeBridge requires transparency for their margin calc, we should do itemized SKUs with a reconciliation appendix.

- Tax and marketplace fees: recommend we exclude reseller uplift from marketplace list price to avoid double counting fees in passback calculations. Naomi, please confirm the standard passback waterwall we should share with procurement.

Proposed next step: share a 2-column pricing sheet (consolidated vs itemized) + suggested uplift table for EdgeBridge. If they insist on a contractual percentage cap, legal will need a one-sentence addendum.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Channel Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Alyssa sent this along but procurement wanted to highlight: when a consolidated SKU is used on GCP private pricing, the marketplace will only surface a single SKU in their billing export; downstream systems that expect seat-level detail may break.

Irene's note: for GCP private offers we can map consolidated SKU -> internal breakdown in our reporting, but we need to include a reconciliation appendix in the PO to allow their finance to match charges. For AWS, consolidated SKU mapping is straightforward. Also note: GCP requires a minimum SKU description length in the private offer metadata, so keep the SKU name descriptive.

-- Irene Choi
Principal Product Manager (Marketplace Integrations)
Redwood Inference

Alyssa — appreciate the requirements doc. We've pulled the numbers and attached a polished two-option matrix: consolidated vs itemized (see pricing_model_v2.xlsx). Summary of the recommended commercial structure: 

1) Offer A — Consolidated SKU (recommended for simplicity)
   - List price: $480k / year
   - Suggested reseller uplift allowance: up to 22% for first-year introductory concession
   - Reconciliation appendix included for GCP mapping

2) Offer B — Itemized SKUs (recommended if EdgeBridge needs line-level visibility)
   - Compute SKU + Inference tokens SKU + Support SKU itemized, combined list equivalent: $495k / year
   - Uplift table as Ben suggested (sheet: uplift_table)

We recommend presenting both to procurement and asking which they prefer; if they push contractual cap language, legal will add the one-sentence addendum limiting reseller uplift to "not exceed X% as agreed in this PO" — we typically leave X as the negotiated number (e.g., 22%).

Next steps: Connor — if you can confirm final preference by tomorrow we'll prepare an updated private_offer_template.docx and a DocuSign-ready PO. Alyssa — I've created a placeholder DocuSign link for the PO draft.

Naomi Feldman
